label: copy-phase steps with input w/r/a/t (low precision, no clean rule)
explanation: Fires almost only in the delimiter and copy phases (99.9% of mass); never in the original phase except a few steps at t=2-3. It fires most often on early recall positions (recall_idx 0-4 hold about 90% of mass). Inputs w, r, a, t (5x lift) and <DEL> are enriched, and outputs k/o and next outputs 1/f/q are also enriched. But firing is sparse inside every slice: only about 10% of copy-phase steps with input w/r/a/t are active, and adding output-token or next-output conditions gives F1 of 0.23 at best. The top activations look like specific (input, output) bigram pairs (r->o, d->k, t->w, a->r, w->n), spread over many tokens. The recorded predicate gets about 55% recall and 60% mass at about 10% precision. Magnitude is higher in long sequences (L=9 holds 34% of mass). No compact explanation found.
